root_motivation: Joe's directive (2026-09-05): use the wiki more. The capture half is now habit — durable decisions get an entity page (see wiki/entities/Fleet Build Automation.md, the first page filed under the new rule). The retrieval half does not exist. recall has five hooks wired into ~/.claude/settings.json (recall-session-start.sh, recall-user-prompt.sh, recall-search-inject.sh, and friends), so Claude memories arrive unbidden; the wiki has zero, so wiki pages arrive never. A knowledge base that is only consulted deliberately decays into an archive. The vault already carries the failure signature: `summa lint` counts 185 orphan pages nothing links to and nothing reads.
user_persona: UNSPECIFIED — no existing intent card to carry forward from; set by hand (intent-card-refresh.sh cannot source this from a PRD).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the current vault, When `summa relevant "how does build start on redbaron"` runs, Then Fleet Build Automation is rank 1 and the output shows its title, relative path, and a one-line summary.
Given a query matching nothing, When `summa relevant` runs, Then stdout is empty and exit is 0.
Given a page with unparseable frontmatter in wiki/, When `summa relevant` runs, Then the page is skipped and the command still succeeds.
Given a fresh session, When the first user prompt fires the hook, Then at most 5 pages and at most 1200 bytes are injected with the `summa: relevant wiki pages` prefix.
Given the same session, When a second prompt fires the hook, Then it emits nothing.
Given a machine without summa on PATH, When the hook fires, Then it emits nothing and exits 0.
Given a 5KB prompt passed via --stdin, When `summa relevant --stdin` runs, Then it returns the same ranking as the argv form for an equivalent query.
Given the ranked output, When --format json is set, Then it parses as a JSON array of {title, path, summary, score}.
Given --explain, When it runs, Then each listed page shows its score broken into title/body/recency components.
